source.title: Extending Factor Graphs so as to Unify Directed and Undirected Graphical Models
source.venue: Proc. 19th Conf. on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence (UAI 2003)

confidence_rationale: Direction convention for the Q-079 novelty question: 'weakens' = weakens the distinct-novel-object (ANSWERED-POSITIVE) reading by showing an existing formalism already covers a needed capacity. High mapping fidelity: factor graphs are a canonical, well-understood substrate; the unification of directed (Bayes-net) and undirected (MRF) models on ONE graph is exactly capacities (a) directed evidence update + (b) cyclic coherence under a single object. Confidence held below 0.8 only because Frey's factor graph alone does not deliver (c) structure birth/death or (d) scale.
failure_signatures: A single static factor graph does not natively perform latent-node birth/death/merge/split (capacity c) -- structure is assumed specified.
Factor graphs do not natively provide granularity/scale shift (capacity d) without an explicit multiscale construction layered on top.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Factor graphs subsume both Bayesian networks (directed) and Markov random fields (undirected) in a single representation, and a common sum-product / message-passing algorithm performs inference over both.
mapping.ree_translation: DLIF capacities (a) directed evidence update and (b) cyclic coherence constraint are NOT two separate formalisms needing a new unifying object -- the factor graph already unifies them. The DLIF cluster's 'directed-update + cyclic-coherence' pairing (pilot P1) is the standard factor-graph offering.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Frey's result covers only capacities (a)+(b). It says nothing about (c) latent-node dynamics, (d) scale shift, action coupling, or residue. It weakens the claim that (a)+(b) jointly is novel; it does not by itself collapse the full DLIF combination.
mapping.source_context: Probabilistic graphical-model theory; no agent, no neural substrate.

confidence_components.notes: Canonical, heavily cited result. Transfer risk low because the claim is purely about representational equivalence, which transfers exactly to REE's cognifold (a typed signed state-space = a typed factor graph).
